overview: In the Owen Defence 1.e4 b6 2.d4 Black plays 2...Ba6, the Guatemala move, to trade off White's light-squared bishop if it develops to d3 or e2, a trappy way to disrupt White's development. White simply plays 3.Bxa6 Nxa6 4.Nf3 or Qe2 and enjoys a centre and space advantage. It is a rare, offbeat sideline rated slightly worse for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Take the bishop with Bxa6 or play Nf3 and Nc3 and keep a pawn centre
Use the e4/d4 space advantage to build an attack

black_ideas.idea: Trade the light-squared bishops and hit the centre with ...e6, ...Nf6 and ...c5
Aim for ...Qe7 and ...Nf6 with quick piece play

typical_structures.structure: White pawn centre on e4/d4 against Black fianchetto pawns, a Pirc/Alekhine-style set-up

character.notes: Black plays an eccentric set-up; White gets a normal edge. Balanced.

soundness.notes: Slightly unsound for Black but not refuted; White gets an easy edge.

structure.notes: White's centre against Black's hypermodern pieces, left in tension: Flexible.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever choose it; offbeat.

level.notes: Easy for White; Black needs careful play. Intermediate.

character.reason: Offbeat but not forcing; White enjoys an easy edge.
